summary: Recent updates to Firefox's integration of **WebRTC**, the technology behind video calls, have introduced several enhancements aimed at improving both performance and reliability. Key changes include implementing **RTCPeerConnection** retransmission stats, allowing better tracking of lost and retransmitted video packets, which can lead to smoother video calls. Furthermore, maintaining hardware decoding for H.264 video when no software decoder is available ensures users benefit from optimal performance even in low-resource situations. Additional tweaks, such as suppressing the transmission of unnecessary DTMF (dual-tone multi-frequency signaling) signals and refining how video data is processed, contribute to a more efficient and stable calling experience. Overall, these updates matter because they enhance the quality and reliability of online communication through Firefox.
